deploymentEvidence.observedExcerpt: Official thUSD core contracts: sthUSD 0xA808Bc9775cb41c52C7842f8b50427fE7A770326; sthUSD logic 0x342487F9Fe31d199Dda8C89a1c34cc647c5A7dC3. Etherscan repeats current implementation.

devdoc.details: This contract implements an upgradeable proxy. It is upgradeable because calls are delegated to an implementation address that can be changed. This address is stored in storage in the location specified by https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967[EIP1967], so that it doesn't conflict with the storage layout of the implementation behind the proxy.

AddressEmptyCode(address).details: There's no code at `target` (it is not a contract).

ERC1967InvalidImplementation(address).details: The `implementation` of the proxy is invalid.

ERC1967NonPayable().details: An upgrade function sees `msg.value > 0` that may be lost.

FailedInnerCall().details: A call to an address target failed. The target may have reverted.

Upgraded(address).details: Emitted when the implementation is upgraded.

constructor.details: Initializes the upgradeable proxy with an initial implementation specified by `implementation`. If `_data` is nonempty, it's used as data in a delegate call to `implementation`. This will typically be an encoded function call, and allows initializing the storage of the proxy like a Solidity constructor. Requirements: - If `data` is empty, `msg.value` must be zero.

deploymentEvidence.bindingExplanation: Official current logic table, Sourcify EIP1967Proxy resolution and Etherscan implementation link independently agree. Explorer proxy source says Similar Match; implementation Sourcify match statuses are preserved literally, without promoting explorer proxy status.

ERC20InsufficientAllowance(address,uint2.details: Indicates a failure with the `spender`’s `allowance`. Used in transfers.

params.allowance: Amount of tokens a `spender` is allowed to operate with.
params.needed: Minimum amount required to perform a transfer.
params.spender: Address that may be allowed to operate on tokens without being their owner.

ERC20InsufficientBalance(address,uint256.details: Indicates an error related to the current `balance` of a `sender`. Used in transfers.

params.balance: Current balance for the interacting account.
params.needed: Minimum amount required to perform a transfer.
params.sender: Address whose tokens are being transferred.

ERC20InvalidApprover(address).details: Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used in approvals.

ERC20InvalidReceiver(address).details: Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.

params.receiver: Address to which tokens are being transferred.

ERC20InvalidSender(address).details: Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.

params.sender: Address whose tokens are being transferred.

ERC20InvalidSpender(address).details: Indicates a failure with the `spender` to be approved. Used in approvals.

params.spender: Address that may be allowed to operate on tokens without being their owner.

ERC4626ExceededMaxMint(address,uint256,u.details: Attempted to mint more shares than the max amount for `receiver`.

ERC4626ExceededMaxRedeem(address,uint256.details: Attempted to redeem more shares than the max amount for `receiver`.

ERC4626ExceededMaxWithdraw(address,uint2.details: Attempted to withdraw more assets than the max amount for `receiver`.

SafeERC20FailedOperation(address).details: An operation with an ERC-20 token failed.

UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext().details: The call is from an unauthorized context.

UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID(bytes32).details: The storage `slot` is unsupported as a UUID.

Approval(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when the allowance of a `spender` for an `owner` is set by a call to {approve}. `value` is the new allowance.

EIP712DomainChanged().details: MAY be emitted to signal that the domain could have changed.

Initialized(uint64).details: Triggered when the contract has been initialized or reinitialized.

Paused(address).details: Emitted when the pause is triggered by `account`.

Transfer(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when `value` tokens are moved from one account (`from`) to another (`to`). Note that `value` may be zero.

DOMAIN_SEPARATOR().details: Returns the domain separator used in the encoding of the signature for {permit}, as defined by {EIP712}.

acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `value` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

eip712Domain().details: returns the fields and values that describe the domain separator used by this contract for EIP-712 signature.

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

nonces(address).details: Returns the current nonce for `owner`. This value must be included whenever a signature is generated for {permit}. Every successful call to {permit} increases ``owner``'s nonce by one. This prevents a signature from being used multiple times.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

permit(address,address,uint256,uint256,u.details: Sets `value` as the allowance of `spender` over ``owner``'s tokens, given ``owner``'s signed approval. IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction ordering also apply here. Emits an {Approval} event. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future. - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner` over the EIP712-formatted function arguments. - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}). For more information on the signature format, see the https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612#specification[relevant EIP section]. CAUTION: See Security Considerations above.

previewRedeem(uint256).custom:deprecated: use maxWithdraw/maxRedeem which return actual claimable amounts based on redeem requests

previewWithdraw(uint256).custom:deprecated: use maxWithdraw/maxRedeem which return actual claimable amounts based on redeem requests

proxiableUUID().details: Implementation of the ERC-1822 {proxiableUUID} function. This returns the storage slot used by the implementation. It is used to validate the implementation's compatibility when performing an upgrade. IMPORTANT: A proxy pointing at a proxiable contract should not be considered proxiable itself, because this risks bricking a proxy that upgrades to it, by delegating to itself until out of gas. Thus it is critical that this function revert if invoked through a proxy. This is guaranteed by the `notDelegated` modifier.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.

upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes).details: Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `newImplementation`, and subsequently execute the function call encoded in `data`. Calls {_authorizeUpgrade}. Emits an {Upgraded} event.

deposit(uint256,address).notice: ERC-4626 Deposit Overrides (paused when contract is paused)

maxDeposit(address).notice: ERC4626 View Overrides (include check for paused state and claimable redeems)

previewRedeem(uint256).notice: Previews return 0 since actual claimable amounts are determined by the redeem request logic, not a calculation based on total assets/shares

previewWithdraw(uint256).notice: Previews return 0 since actual claimable amounts are determined by the redeem request logic, not a calculation based on total assets/shares

selectedFunctions.label: Theo Stake thUSD for sthUSD
warnings: Static deployment/source inventory only: not a fresh RPC/runtime/storage identity, current configuration, liquidity, backing, balance, financial-safety or successful-execution guarantee. Canonical calldata, grants, allowances, pause scopes and independent execution controls remain mandatory. All admitted functions are nonpayable; send zero native value.

Ethereum sthUSD ERC1967 UUPS proxy 0xA808Bc9775cb41c52C7842f8b50427fE7A770326, current official/Sourcify/explorer implementation 0x342487F9Fe31d199Dda8C89a1c34cc647c5A7dC3. Owner-controlled upgrades can replace behavior. The vault is distinct from Theo thBILL/metal products and bridged OFTs, none of which are admitted.

Underlying is 6-decimal thUSD (0xa3fE5c7596024E6811E14F029937D5bd8Ae485b3), not USDC/USDT; sthUSD shares also use 6 decimals. Deposit/mint transfer caller thUSD via allowance and issue receiver shares. No caller min-shares/max-assets or deadline parameter exists; very small inherited ERC4626 deposits can round to zero shares.

initiateRedeem burns owner shares immediately, fixes underlying thUSD at the then-current conversion, and books the request to msg.sender, not owner. If delegated, existing owner-to-caller share allowance is consumed. Claim custody/control belongs to the initiator; select owner/caller deliberately. Pending amounts stop earning. Repeating initiation merges with and restarts the lockup for the entire caller request.

withdraw/redeem are mature request claims, not synchronous ERC4626 exits. owner must equal msg.sender (the request holder); allowance cannot authorize a different claim caller. A prior initiateRedeem and elapsed claimableTimestamp are required. Official reference reports 5-day lockup at its review; owner can set future request lockup up to 30 days. Current lockup/paused state is not attested.

previewWithdraw/previewRedeem deliberately always return zero; use booked currentRedeemRequest/maxWithdraw/maxRedeem to interpret claims. Partial redeem rounds assets down; partial withdraw rounds request shares up, and if rounding consumes all shares pays all remaining assets. Full claims pay all remaining request assets. Burning the last live shares assigns remaining non-pending vault assets, including unvested yield, to that request.

Vault operations and claims require not paused; guardian pause and owner unpause remain independent controls, while token transfers are not paused. Ordinary vault calls do not consult TheoWhitelist; direct thUSD mint/redemption is a separate whitelisted signed-order system and is excluded. Legal eligibility is not conferred by catalog membership.

totalAssets excludes unvested yield and booked redemption assets. Distributor-supplied yield vests over configurable duration up to 365 days. No explicit deposit/claim fee appears in reviewed vault source; gas and external-system fees are separate. No permit, ownership/role authorization, yield distribution, UUPS upgrade, arbitrary executor or bridge admitted.
